from.place: Opening sentence, Choose a compactification c=(j,p): the inherited coherent cone-comparison foundation; strict versus homotopy fibers of its right-fibration lift space. The current main-20261015 blueprint has no separate right-fibration statement.

proof.text: Fix $x,y\in B$ and $e'\in E_y$. By [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], the arrow mapping space $A=U_B(x,y)$ is Kan and the right-pinch inclusion $j_B:\operatorname{Map}_B(x,y)\to A$ is a natural homotopy equivalence. By [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-fibers], $E_x$ is Kan (apply it with both right fibrations equal to $p$). Define $L$ in degree $n$ to consist of pairs $(a,h)$, where $a:\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\to B$ is an $n$-simplex of $A$ and $h:\Delta^1\times\Delta^n\to E$ satisfies $ph=a$ and $h|_{\{1\}\times\Delta^n}=e'$. Restriction defines simplicial maps $r:L\to A$, $(a,h)\mapsto a$, and $s:L\to E_x$, $(a,h)\mapsto h|_{\{0\}\times\Delta^n}$. All equalities at endpoints mean constant simplices, not merely their vertices, as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones].

source.place: Proposition 4.6.5.10 and the explicit arrow-space construction; Kan fibers are the cited existing right-fibration-fibers statement.

proof.text: The inclusion $\{1\}=\Lambda_1^1\hookrightarrow\Delta^1$ is one of the generating right horns. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-right-fibration-exponentiation] to $p$ and this inclusion. Its trivial Kan fibration $\rho$ pulls back along $A\to\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\times_B E$, $a\mapsto(a,e')$, to exactly $r:L\to A$. To lift a boundary against $r$, lift its $h$-coordinate against $\rho$ with the prescribed $a$-coordinate, so $r$ is a trivial Kan fibration. By [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms], $r$ lifts every degreewise injection. Fill a projected horn in the Kan space $A$, then lift that horn against $r$; thus $L$ is Kan and $r$ is a Kan fibration. By [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion], $r$ is a weak equivalence and every fiber $r^{-1}(a)$ is contractible. For a vertex $a:x\to y$, this fiber is precisely the whole space of lifts with target $e'$, and $s$ records their sources in $E_x$.

source.place: Proposition 4.2.5.4 with the final-vertex horn; boundary lifting and the cited trivial-Kan criterion.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] to $\varnothing\hookrightarrow A$ to choose a section $\sigma:A\to L$ of $r$. Define $\operatorname{Sec}(r)_n$ to be maps $u:A\times\Delta^n\to L$ with $ru=\operatorname{pr}_A$. A boundary in this section simplicial set is a partial map on $A\times\partial\Delta^n$; the same lifting lemma extends it across the degreewise injection into $A\times\Delta^n$, including $n=0$. Hence $\operatorname{Sec}(r)\to\Delta^0$ lifts all boundaries, lifts all horns by that lemma, and is contractible by [lem-cbc-kan-fibration-fiber-criterion]. Put $t_A=s\sigma$ and $t_{e'}=t_Aj_B$. At a vertex $a$, this map sends $a$ to the source $a^*e'$ of the chosen lift. Since the choices are sections on the entire simplicial set $A$, their contractible space retains every higher compatibility, rather than selecting unrelated lifts for individual edges.

source.place: Section space of the explicit trivial Kan fibration; the parameterized extension argument is written out.

proof.text: Write $E_{e'}^{\mathrm{arr}}=\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,E)\times_{\operatorname{ev}_1,E}\{e'\}$. Degree by degree there is an equality $L=E_x\times_E E_{e'}^{\mathrm{arr}}$: an arrow in $E$ with target constantly $e'$ and source in $E_x$ projects to exactly an element of $U_B(x,y)$. By [lem-coef-infinity-arrow-target-right-fibration], source evaluation $E_{e'}^{\mathrm{arr}}\to E$ is a right fibration. A lifting problem for its pullback $s:L\to E_x$ lifts by applying that statement with the prescribed base simplex in $E_x$, so $s$ is a right fibration. Apply [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber] to $s$ with its Kan base $E_x$. Its strict fiber over $e$ is exactly $U_E(e,e')$, and its constant-path inclusion gives a natural equivalence $U_E(e,e')\to\operatorname{hofib}_e(s)$.

source.place: Proposition 4.6.4.13 pulled back to the source fiber; the general space-fiber comparison is cited separately.

proof.text: Since $r\sigma=\mathrm{id}_A$ and $r$ is a weak equivalence, $\sigma:A\to L$ is a weak equivalence. The square with top map $\sigma$, vertical maps $t_A$ and $s$, and bottom map $\mathrm{id}_{E_x}$ commutes strictly. Apply [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection]: its forward implication gives $\operatorname{hofib}_e(t_A)\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_e(s)$ for every $e\in E_x$. Apply that statement once more to the square with top map $j_B$, vertical maps $t_{e'}=t_Aj_B$ and $t_A$, and bottom identity. The top map is a homotopy equivalence by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison], so $\operatorname{hofib}_e(t_{e'})\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_e(t_A)$. Together with step 4 and the natural pinch equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_E(e,e')\simeq U_E(e,e')$, this is the asserted equivalence. The homotopy fibers here use paths from the image to $e$ exactly as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]; no simplicial path-reversal map is asserted.

source.place: The cited existing homotopy-fiber-detection statement, twice with identity base; pinch comparison is Proposition 4.6.5.10.

proof.text: For a base change $f:B'\to B$ and vertices $x',y'$ over $x,y$, put $E'=B'\times_BE$ and use the point of $E'_{y'}$ induced by $e'$. Set $A'=U_{B'}(x',y')$. The degreewise formulas in step 1 identify $E'_{x'}=E_x$ and $L'=A'\times_A L$: the base arrow in $B'$ supplies the missing coordinate of a lifted arrow in $E'$. A section $\sigma$ therefore induces $\sigma'(a')=(a',\sigma(fa'))$, and $s'\sigma'=s\sigma f$ strictly. For sections chosen independently, a boundary of comparisons is a map $A'\times\partial\Delta^n\to L'$ over $A'$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-trivial-kan-lifts-monomorphisms] to the inclusion $A'\times\partial\Delta^n\hookrightarrow A'\times\Delta^n$ to extend it; this also works after multiplying both sides by any parameter simplicial set $K$. These extensions give the higher comparisons in the section space of step 3. The pinch maps commute with $f$ by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. The constant-path comparison of [lem-cbc-right-fibration-space-fiber] and the homotopy-fiber maps of [lem-coef-spaces-homotopy-fiber-detection] commute with these coordinate maps. Varying $e$ uses the same homotopy-fiber families; varying $e'$ is included by pulling $\rho$ back along $A\times E_y\to\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,B)\times_B E$, $(a,v)\mapsto(a,v)$, to a trivial Kan fibration $r_{\mathrm{tot}}:L_{\mathrm{tot}}\to A\times E_y$. A boundary in its section space is a map $(A\times E_y)\times\partial\Delta^n\to L_{\mathrm{tot}}$ over $A\times E_y$; the cited monomorphism-lifting lemma extends it to $(A\times E_y)\times\Delta^n$. A section therefore gives transport on the entire family $A\times E_y$, and its restrictions give the choices for each $e'$ with all compatibilities. These constructions prove pullback compatibility and naturality on all simplices, with the contractible choices understood as in step 3.

title: Mapping spaces and transport in a right fibration
statement: Use quasicategories, right-pinched mapping spaces and homotopy fibers as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $E,B$ be quasicategories and $p:E\to B$ a right fibration, meaning it lifts every horn $\Lambda_i^n\hookrightarrow\Delta^n$ with $n\geq1$ and $0<i\leq n$. Write $E_x=\{x\}\times_B E$. For $e\in E_x$, $e'\in E_y$ and an edge $a:x\to y$, lifts of $a$ with target $e'$ give an object $a^*e'\in E_x$, with a contractible space of compatible choices. These lifts define a map of spaces $t_{e'}:\operatorname{Map}_B(x,y)\to E_x$, up to coherent homotopy. There is a natural equivalence $\operatorname{Map}_E(e,e')\simeq\operatorname{hofib}_e(t_{e'})$. This description is compatible with pullback of $p$ along simplicial functors and retains all higher homotopies.

source.place: Agent formulation of the right-fibration specialization of Proposition 5.1.2.1 (01TL), cartesian mapping squares, using Proposition 5.1.4.15 (every edge of a right fibration is cartesian) and Remark 5.1.3.8 (01U5), uniqueness of lifts. A cartesian lift of a identifies the mapping fiber over a with paths from e to a*e′ in E_x. This generic transport statement is not attributed to the unrelated cone criterion at 02NR.
